title: Page: from 20 s, 30–40% of requests fail and p99 goes up to about 3 s.
explain: The whole database is 20× slower. Reads that miss the cache and all writes wait for it and fail at the API → db timeout (500 ms); the waiting requests hold the API's slots, and the requests behind them queue. Open the database's metrics: utilisation and the queue are much higher than before, but it does not fail itself (the API that calls it gives up).
hint: The database is slow, but it is not down and it is not full. Requests fail because the 500 ms timeout is now shorter than one write, and the waiting requests fill the API slots. Raise the API server's concurrency (for example 64) and make the timeouts long enough to get the reply (API → db 3 s, load balancer → API 4 s): users wait longer, but their requests do not fail. Another way: shorten the API → db timeout and turn on the fallback response.
